recon.notes: Added 2026-10-18 at the owner’s request: Bears Sitges Club’s own ticket shop (the Bears Sitges Week programme’s ticket links point at bearsevents.com /product/ pages, three of them as typos — see bears-sitges-week.json). The Tribe calendar on this host carries the ticketed festival-week extras (Sunset Tea Dance, Drag Brunch Bear Edition, VIP Zone), not the whole programme, and only around the September week: six rows in its whole history across two editions, one of them cancelled. data/promoters.json maps bearsevents.com (urlPatterns) and the organizer name "Bears Events" (alias) to the Bears Sitges Club entry, so nothing here is a second promoter. Timezone on every row is the pseudo-zone "UTC+0": the feed reader only adopts IANA names (Area/City), so a row from here takes the city’s zone, Europe/Madrid, which is what the wall-clock times mean.

coverage.basis: Two independent doors agree the site publishes zero upcoming events on 2026-10-18: the listing page’s own empty state ("There are no upcoming events.", door 1) and the REST route’s default window (total 0, door 2). The archive read (door 3) reconciles the page’s "Latest Past Events" block and counts the past listings: six rows, 2025-05-02 … 2026-09-13, all past — counted, not enumerated. The shop’s /product/ pages are WooCommerce products (tickets), not calendar rows, and were not read.

openQuestions.q: When the 2027 rows appear here they will also be lines of the bearssitges.org programme (bears-sitges-week.json documents the tea dance and the drag brunch from the programme text, with flyer-vs-text time deltas). Which copy should win the time — the shop’s feed (structured, ticketed) or the programme line? Both parsers are curated-promoter Bears Sitges Club sources.

Three list rows, one record: the AI read of the "Latest Past Events" block (run 20261018-111437) produced a single "BEAR WEEK DRAG BRUNCH" dated 2025-09-14 with the 2024 preview flyer’s venue text and city unknown, instead of three rows with their <time datetime> dates — the same missing Tribe list-row reader as sitges-bear-cave.json raises. Until the feed has upcoming rows, this page yields that chimera on every run; it is a past record, so the calendar never sees it as a write, but it sits in the results as "new".

The feed’s rows say timezone "UTC+0" with Sitges wall-clock times. The reader drops non-IANA zone strings and the city’s zone applies, which is right here; is that worth a log line when it happens, so a site that really means UTC is noticed?
